documents.title: Academic Integrity
documents.summary: University AI academic-integrity page. Treats unauthorized or uncited AI use as plagiarism, requires citation and disclosure, and lists CES principles on integrity, data protection, transparency and accountability. Faculty define use; students follow.
documents.stance_why: Says AI use 'must follow the instructions of the course and instructor' and bans unauthorized use, so the document sets no single stance and defers to instructors.

units.why: States that members must 'complete their own work and demonstrate their own understanding'; addressed to all community members and about owning submitted work, so P29.
units.anchor: expected to complete their own work and demonstrate their own understanding

units.why: Classifies 'Using AI-generated content without permission or proper citation' as plagiarism, so it is treated as misconduct (P36), not merely a disclosure rule.
units.anchor: is considered a form of plagiarism

units.why: Says students must not 'rely on AI tools to complete academic tasks unless clearly authorized'; this sets a default of no AI when not authorized, which is the fallback rule (P06) rather than P01 because permission can come from the instructor.
units.anchor: not to rely on AI tools to complete academic tasks unless clearly authorized

units.why: 'AI use must follow the instructions of the course and instructor' hands the rule to each instructor/course, so P04.
units.anchor: AI use must follow the instructions of the course and instructor.

units.why: 'If AI use is permitted, it must be properly cited using an approved style' is a citation requirement on submissions, P24.
units.anchor: If AI use is permitted, it must be properly cited using an approved style

units.why: 'Unauthorized or misuse of Generative AI may lead to academic penalties and disciplinary action' links misuse to sanctions; penalties are not concrete so P36 rather than P37.
units.anchor: Unauthorized or misuse of Generative AI may lead to academic penalties and disciplinary action.

units.why: 'you must cite them appropriately' when the instructor allows AI tools; a citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: you must cite them appropriately
units.frag_start: If your instructor allows the use

units.why: The university 'has published an AI Citation Style Guide' showing MLA, APA and Chicago formats; this supplies the citation format for P24 disclosure.
units.anchor: shows how to cite AI-generated content in MLA, APA, and Chicago formats

units.why: Gives the reason for citing: it 'protects you from unintentional plagiarism and shows academic honesty'; a rationale attached to the disclosure rule, so P24.
units.anchor: Citing AI tools protects you from unintentional plagiarism and shows academic honesty.

units.why: Tells students unsure how to cite to ask an instructor or librarian. P10 covers asking before using AI, not asking how to cite, so no type fits well.
units.anchor: If you're unsure how to cite something, ask your instructor or a librarian for help.
units.frag_start: If you're unsure how to cite
units.uncovered_note: Students unsure how to cite AI are told to seek help from instructor or librarian.

units.why: The Integrity principle 'Use AI to support learning, not to shortcut it' limits AI because shortcutting undermines learning, so P41.
units.anchor: Use AI to support learning, not to shortcut it.

units.why: 'Verify the accuracy of AI output' tells students to check AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Verify the accuracy of AI output.

units.why: 'Never enter personal, private, or sensitive data into AI tools' is a data-protection prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: Never enter personal, private, or sensitive data into AI tools.

units.why: Students should use only tools 'approved or well-vetted by the university', i.e. prefer vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: or well-vetted by the university.
units.policy: Use only tools that are approved or well-vetted by the university.

units.why: 'Always disclose when you use AI in your work' is the Transparency principle, a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: Always disclose when you use AI in your work.

units.why: 'Be honest about what you created and what AI generated' asks students to distinguish own and AI contributions in disclosure, P24 (not P27 because no place-marking is required).
units.anchor: Be honest about what you created and what AI generated.

units.why: 'You are responsible for how you use AI' places accountability on the student, P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for how you use AI.

units.why: 'When in doubt, ask' tells students unsure of a use to ask first, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask.

units.why: The university 'encourages students to follow the CES AI Guiding Principles'; an institution-level principles framework, P56.
units.anchor: BYU–Idaho encourages students to follow the

units.why: Faculty 'should clearly define AI tool usage', i.e. state expectations to students, P09 (not P04 since it concerns communicating).
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define AI tool usage

units.why: Same sentence says faculty should 'stay apprised of AI usage in the workforce, and align activities to prepare students for employment', a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: stay apprised of AI usage in the workforce, and align activities

units.why: Students 'should follow the instructor’s guidelines for AI use', delegating to the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Students should follow the instructor’s guidelines for AI use

units.why: Students should 'genuinely learn rather than shortcut the learning process'; skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: seek to genuinely learn rather than shortcut the learning process

units.why: Students should 'be transparent about when AI tools are used', disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: be transparent about when AI tools are used

units.why: 'Students are responsible for ensuring their work reflects their own understanding and effort', ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for ensuring their work reflects their own understanding and effort

units.why: Frames AI integrity religiously: 'Using AI responsibly is part of that growth'; a statement of purpose and principles, P56.
units.anchor: Using AI responsibly is part of that growth.

documents.title: AI in the Syllabus
tiers: Stoplight: RED disallow / YELLOW limited use / GREEN active application
AI Assessment Scale: No AI / AI for Ideas / AI for Feedback / AI for Content / AI-Led
documents.summary: University page requiring every syllabus to carry a generative AI statement and giving faculty a statement wizard, two tier frameworks, and citation and declaration resources.
documents.stance_why: Requires a syllabus statement but says 'Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely', and offers Stoplight and Assessment Scale tiers.

units.why: 'Every course syllabus ... is expected to include a statement regarding the use of generative AI' requires an AI statement in each syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: Every course syllabus at BYU-Idaho is expected to include a statement regarding the use

units.why: 'Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely' leaves the choice to each instructor and only requires clarity, P04.
units.anchor: Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely

units.why: Explains the purpose of the syllabus statement: 'Clear communication clarifies student expectations, promotes academic integrity, and models the transparency we expect'. Closest is P09 since it justifies the requirement.
units.anchor: Clear communication clarifies student expectations, promotes academic integrity

units.why: Quotes Elder Bednar that technology 'must not entice us to circumvent the struggle required for deep learning'; protects productive struggle, P41.
units.anchor: it must not entice us to circumvent the struggle required for deep learning

units.why: 'We use AI judiciously to help students become sound thinkers, skilled collaborators, and effective communicators' states the institutional purpose, P56.
units.anchor: We use AI judiciously to help students become sound thinkers

units.why: Offers an 'AI Statement Wizard' to guide faculty in drafting a syllabus statement; faculty support for setting policy, P63.
units.anchor: a BYU-Idaho AI Statement Wizard that will guide you through some thought exercises

units.why: Stoplight Level One RED 'Disallow. All work must be human-created' is a named tier of AI use, P05; it is the prohibit tier.
units.anchor: Disallow. All work must be human-created.

units.why: Stoplight Level Two YELLOW 'Limited Use. Specific tools permitted for defined tasks' is a named middle tier, P05.
units.anchor: Limited Use. Specific tools permitted for defined tasks.

units.why: Stoplight Level Three GREEN 'Active Application. Intentional use of AI tools expected' is the top tier where AI use is expected, P05.
units.anchor: Active Application. Intentional use of AI tools expected.

units.why: The AI Assessment Scale lists five levels (No AI, AI for Ideas, AI for Feedback, AI for Content, AI-Led), a second tier scheme, P05.
units.anchor: AI for Ideas Brainstorming & outlining

units.why: Offers a framework 'to help them declare and reflect on their use of AI', a student-disclosure aid for instructors to share, P24.
units.anchor: help them declare and reflect on their use of AI.

units.why: Offers a style guide 'to help them cite their use of AI' from the Writing Lab, supporting citation requirement P24.
units.anchor: A style guide to share with students to help them cite their use of AI.

units.why: Offers a webinar for faculty on academic integrity and AI; learning support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: A webinar by author James Lang to help faculty learn more strategies

documents.title: CSE Generative AI Usage Policy
documents.summary: CSE department policy that encourages students to use generative AI for coding, debugging, ideas and learning as a complement to their own effort. All works must carry an AI-use statement with an IEEE-style citation.
documents.stance_why: The policy 'encourages students to utilize AI tools' for coding, ideas and learning, with required disclosure.

units.why: Summary says the policy 'encourages students to utilize AI tools for enhancing learning, creativity, and productivity', a default of encouragement, P02.
units.anchor: It encourages students to utilize AI tools for enhancing learning, creativity, and productivity

units.why: Students are encouraged to 'Explore and use generative AI tools to assist with coding tasks'; broad permission to use AI for code, P02 (not P16, no conditions on code amount).
units.anchor: Explore and use generative AI tools to assist with coding tasks

units.why: Likens AI use to 'pair programming, tutoring sessions, or one-on-one meetings with professors'; treats AI as a collaborator, P45.
units.anchor: Approach the use of generative AI tools with the same collaborative spirit as pair programming

units.why: 'Use generative AI as a learning resource to understand different approaches to coding' is AI as a tutor for concepts, P12.
units.anchor: Use generative AI as a learning resource to understand different approaches to coding and problem-solving.

units.why: 'Maintain an active role in decision-making throughout the automation process' keeps the student as the primary decision-maker, P32.
units.anchor: Maintain an active role in decision-making throughout the automation process.

units.why: Encourages AI 'for code completion, debugging, and optimization'; debugging help is the closest type, P13.
units.anchor: Use generative AI tools for code completion, debugging, and optimization

units.why: 'Use generative AI as a source of inspiration to explore novel ideas' is brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: Use generative AI as a source of inspiration to explore novel ideas and innovative solutions.
units.frag_start: Use generative AI as a source

units.why: 'Employ generative AI to generate diverse perspectives and approaches' is exploring alternative approaches, P15.
units.anchor: generate diverse perspectives and approaches to software development challenges

units.why: Use AI 'as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, personal learning efforts' means AI must not replace the student's thinking, P32.
units.anchor: as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, personal learning efforts
units.frag_start: Embrace generative AI as a tool

units.why: 'Utilize the AI for self-reflection, identifying areas for improvement' is AI as a self-check of knowledge, P14.
units.anchor: Utilize the AI for self-reflection, identifying areas for improvement
units.frag_start: Embrace generative AI as a tool

units.why: 'A statement indicating that AI was used to aid in its production is required in all works' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: AI was used to aid in its production is required in all works.

units.why: Gives an IEEE citation example naming the tool, vendor and date, which fits citing tool and date, P25.
units.anchor: Text generated by ChatGPT, OpenAI, March 7, 2023

units.why: Students 'should indicate what and where' portions were made without AI, an extra disclosure of human-only parts, P24 (not P27 which marks AI-derived code).
units.anchor: students should indicate what and where these portions are in the work.
units.frag_start: If some portions of the work

units.why: 'Treat generative AI as a supplementary learning resource' frames AI as a study aid for insight into approaches, P12.
units.anchor: Treat generative AI as a supplementary learning resource

units.why: 'Personal involvement should be a constant as you use these tools' keeps the student the primary problem-solver, P32.
units.anchor: Personal involvement should be a constant as you use these tools

units.why: Says integrating AI 'will promote an environment ... that fosters creativity' and proficient software developers; departmental commitment to integrate AI, P02.
units.anchor: Integrating generative AI into the department will promote an environment

notes: No school-level policy found; course layer deferred in collect. Ambiguity: P10 vs UNCOVERED for how-to-cite help; P02 used for CSE encouragement of AI code assistance because no code-amount conditions are stated.
